tb21_profile.skill: Configure two real, already-installed system daemons (Postfix MTA + Mailman3) so they interoperate end-to-end: edit /etc config files, wire transport/aliases/LMTP handoff, get local delivery landing in /var/mail mbox, start the services, and drive the join/confirm/leave/post workflow until an eval script passes.
tb21_profile.domain: Linux mail stack - Postfix, Mailman3, SMTP/LMTP, mbox delivery, /etc service configuration, unix users and service startup.
tb21_profile.task_form: Configure-a-service: multi-daemon integration with no code to write, iterated against a provided eval harness.

TMax-15K.reason: Two mail services fail to communicate; fix their config so the SMTP gateway reaches the API, plus parse mail headers and bodies. Same wire-the-daemons-together work.
Restore a mailing-list architecture: SMTP receiver plus worker under process supervision, with unix users and groups created for it.
Stand up an SMTP mailing-list integration alongside other services, all running under one account on chosen ports. Multi-service mail bring-up.
Configure a mailing-list server through its setup tool, make the deployment idempotent, then verify the restored mail spools. Same configure-then-verify-delivery loop.
An SMTP relay writes received mail into a spool directory and a daemon must consume it; getting spool-based mail delivery working end to end.
Fix the orchestration of three cooperating daemons (Nginx, Flask, Redis) so the deployment actually functions. Multi-daemon misconfiguration debugging.
Edit a systemd unit so the web server's user can reach a UNIX socket after restart; service-unit and permission wiring between two daemons.
Edit a pre-installed service's config file and bring two services up correctly before the rest of the work can run. The bare configure-and-start skill.
Generate a postfix-style mailing-list config file with domain and daemon-count keys, then stage worker startup. Mail-server config generation.
Idempotently set up the mail spool environment plus timezone and locale for a mailing-list system; the spool-side prerequisites for delivery.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Make one setting consistent in both a live database and /etc/asterisk/kamailio.conf, starting the service if needed. Config-in-two-places for a telecom daemon.
Reconcile a live Samba AD directory against a config file listing required accounts and OUs; provisioning membership into a running daemon, as with list members.
A healthcheck demands named services running and a user record present; fix until it passes. Same iterate-against-a-checker service bring-up.
Provision named users and organizational units into a running directory service. Account provisioning against a live daemon.
Provision a full LAMP stack with SSL, the right modules and extensions, all enabled and running. Multi-package service configuration.
Free a port held by another process, enable and restart the web daemon, and open the firewall for it. The port-contention half of daemon bring-up.
Install every extension a requirements file lists, configure Apache with SSL, and serve the right pages. Config-driven service setup.
Configure brokers' listeners so cross-datacenter traffic routes correctly; getting listener and transport configuration right between daemons.
Open exactly the ports two running services need and nothing else; reconciling firewall policy with what the daemons actually listen on.
Read every connection detail from a config file and subscribe to a broker topic, appending received messages. Config-driven subscribe-and-receive.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Configure an authoritative DNS daemon and its zone data until an external dig query returns NOERROR with the right record. Identical configure-until-the-protocol-works shape.
Get httpd onto a port sendmail is holding and open it in firewalld permanently and at runtime. Mail daemon port contention plus service bring-up.
Install a master daemon from its vendor repo, set the hostname it needs, and leave it running, listening on its port and enabled at boot.
Change a daemon's port in its /etc config file and make the daemon actually listen there. The minimal edit-config-then-restart-and-verify loop.
Install the package, change a bind directive in /etc/redis/redis.conf, then restart and enable the service. Same package-config-service sequence.
Configure a web stack with specific modules enabled and conflicting ones disabled, directories created and a second daemon running. Multi-daemon config.
Install and configure an nginx plus php-fpm stack with a precise package set. Package-driven service configuration.
Install a daemon from source, create its config directory in the expected place, and start it logging to /var/log. Config-dir plus daemon startup.
Drive a line protocol by hand with netcat: register, join, send, capture the server's replies. Same manual protocol-workflow reasoning as the join/confirm exchange.
Install and run an SSH daemon inside a container with a set password, committed and left running. Install-configure-run a network service.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Fix SMTP STARTTLS negotiation and expose a TLS setting for mail sending; real SMTP client-side protocol and configuration work.
Every configuration path - CLI, config file, environment - fails so the daemon will not start at all. Daemon configuration loading.
A config file named through an environment variable is ignored; the server silently runs with the wrong settings, the classic service-config failure.
parse_address mishandles most bind-address forms, so the daemon binds to the wrong place or not at all. Listener address configuration.
Config file loading reads a default filename instead of the one specified; the specified path must win, exactly as with mailman.cfg.
Socket creation fails while processing the configured addresses; the daemon cannot open its listener.
A protocol parser must reject malformed requests gracefully rather than blowing up; server-side robustness against bad input on the wire.
Email address validation mishandles edge cases; address validity is what a list manager decides membership on.
The arbiter unlinks sockets it should leave alone on stop; daemon lifecycle and socket cleanup semantics.
A config-file section is silently not loaded, so declared settings never take effect. Config-section parsing only.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: A text-protocol server must tolerate a flag its clients prepend; server-side protocol compatibility, the closest thing here to MTA behaviour.
Server-side index validation does not inherit configured credentials; a daemon behaving wrongly because config does not propagate.
A long-running daemon's persistent state file becomes corrupted across restarts; diagnosing a service that fails after deployment.
Subscription and offset-reset state goes inconsistent after an upgrade; a subscribe/track state machine getting out of sync.
How a server handler subscribes to and is notified of connection lifecycle events; protocol-server callback wiring.
A config file does not survive a write-then-reload round trip; rewriting a service config correctly enough that the next read works.
A timestamp reaches email.utils.formatdate already skewed, producing a wrong mail-style header value.
The connector gives up after the first resolved address instead of trying the rest; the fallback behaviour an MTA depends on.
A broker disconnection handler loops retrying instead of giving up; daemon reconnect behaviour under failure.
SSH/SFTP transport behaviour changed between versions and must be reconciled; remote-protocol client configuration.

final_top10.reason: Configure an installed daemon and its data files until a real protocol query against it returns the right answer. Same shape, different protocol.
Two mail-path services are misconfigured and cannot talk; fix the config so mail flows, then parse the messages correctly.
Bring a mailing-list architecture back up: SMTP receiver plus worker under supervision, with the unix accounts it needs.
A mail daemon is squatting the port the target service needs, and the firewall blocks it; resolve both and leave the service reachable.
Stand up an SMTP mailing-list integration together with other services, all running under one account. Multi-service mail bring-up.
Drive a mailing-list server's setup tool to produce its config, make it idempotent, then verify mail actually landed in the spool.
Install a server daemon from its vendor repo, set the hostname it depends on, and leave it running, listening and enabled.
Keep one setting consistent between a live database and an /etc config file, starting the service if it is down. Two-sided daemon configuration.
Install the package, change the bind directive in its /etc config, then restart and enable the service. The core loop of this task.
Real SMTP work: fix STARTTLS negotiation and make the TLS mode configurable. Same protocol, from the sending side.

notes: The shortlist mostly surfaced TMax tasks that merely mention mailing lists while actually asking for Expect scripts, C programs or Rust CLIs - domain match with little skill transfer. The genuine skill here (configure installed daemons via /etc until a protocol workflow succeeds) lives in TerminalWorld, which the retrievers ranked poorly because the TB2.1 text has no overlapping vocabulary with 'configure bind9' or 'change sshd_config'; tw_1060, tw_321921, tw_14495, tw_117157, tw_12554 and tw_138158 were all self-directed finds. tw_321921 is a nice double hit: sendmail holding a port. Nothing anywhere in the pool configures Postfix or Mailman, so no candidate scores 5. SWE-Smith's only real mail item is scrapy's SMTP STARTTLS fix; its gunicorn cluster is the best proxy for 'daemon config loading'. SWE-Rebench is the weakest corpus for this task - it has no mail-server or service-configuration content at all, and its tens top out at 3.
